answer: Homophily dominating. Sampling that moves outward to increasing distances is the DFS-like regime (low return parameter p relative to in-out parameter q, i.e., q < 1). It emphasizes homophily and community structure, where nodes that are close tend to share labels. That fits the reported gains on Flickr and YouTube, which are label-homophilous networks. Structural equivalence, which the BFS-like regime (q > 1) captures by staying in the local neighborhood, would matter more only when node roles or local structural patterns, rather than community membership, drive the labels.
